thought.text: The `/data` volume inherited root ownership from my image. I'll fix the Dockerfile to create `/data` owned by uid 1000 and remove the old empty volume:

reasoning_content:
MinIO can't write to /data. The problem: I set `USER 1000:1000` in my image, but the named volume `/data` (nebu-minio_data) was either created by the previous container run as root, or... wait, the volume was already created in a previous compose run (it was created before minio failed). Docker named volumes are initialized with the filesystem user that the image declares... but the actual issue is that the volume's ownership doesn't match user 1000.

Actually, the official minio image runs as user 1001 (minio-user). In my image I used 1000. The existing volume `nebu-minio_data` was created earlier (in run 2) by a container that started up as user 1000 (my image v1 also had USER 1000), so the contents of /data are owned by uid 1000... and now the container is running as 1000. Hmm, but it's showing "file access denied".

Wait — in run 2, did the minio container even start successfully in the first place? The error in run 2 was about "server" not being found in $PATH — that was the *server* service, not minio. Actually, in the ps output from run 2, nebu-minio-1 was shown as "Created" (it was never started, because the server was the one that failed... no wait, that's wrong).

Hmm, actually in run 2's ps: nebu-minio-1 Created. So in run 2 minio never started (because the server's task creation failed, compose up -d stopped? Actually `docker compose up -d` starts services independently. If minio was "Created" and not "Up", maybe compose interrupted the startup).

Now, in run 3, the minio container is running as user 1000, and the volume... the volume `nebu-minio_data` was created (an empty directory) by the first `docker compose up` attempt. The ownership of the directory on first creation: Docker initializes an empty named volume with the ownership of the image's directory at that path at the time of first mount... actually, when a named volume is mounted into a container for the first time, if the volume is empty, Docker copies the contents and ownership/permissions of the image's directory at that path into the volume. My image declares `VOLUME /data`, and the /data directory created by... — I never even created /data in my Dockerfile! The `VOLUME /data` instruction implicitly creates the directory as root at build time. So the /data that the volume inherits from the image is owned by root:root, and since it's now running as user 1000 → it can't write → "file access denied".

Fix: create /data with uid 1000 ownership in the Dockerfile:
```
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown 1000:1000 /data
```
But the existing volume already has root-owned content (probably just an empty directory). A named volume initialized from an image directory: if the volume was already initialized in run 2 (with root-owned /data from the image), then rebuilding the image won't change the existing volume. The safest thing is: after fixing the image, `docker volume rm nebu_nebu-minio_data` (it's empty/unused), rebuild the image, and start it up. The volume name is probably `nebu-minio_data` (compose name is "nebu" → volume is `nebu-minio_data`).

Alternatively, to completely avoid the uid hassle, I could also drop USER from my image and run as root — but the compose healthcheck and the createbuckets mc client don't care. Running MinIO as root works, but... the official image runs as 1001. Either is fine for local development. But cleaner is: create /data as 1000 in the image, and delete the old volume.

Note that the official minio image actually uses USER 1001:1001, and the /data volume gets chowned via an entrypoint script? No — the official image's Dockerfile: creates a minio-user (1001) and chowns /data. Actually, the official image runs `RUN useradd...`, chowns /data, and then `USER 1001`. When the named volume is first initialized, the /data from the image (owned by 1001) is copied into the volume, so minio can write. My image needs to do the same: create /data owned by 1000, and run as 1000.

Let me rebuild and remove the old volume.

action.command:
set -e
cd /workspace/.local-images/minio
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM alpine:3.20
RUN apk add --no-cache curl
COPY minio /usr/bin/minio
RUN chmod +x /usr/bin/minio && mkdir -p /data && chown 1000:1000 /data && minio --version
USER 1000:1000
VOLUME /data
EXPOSE 9000 9001
ENTRYPOINT ["minio"]
EOF
docker build -q -t minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z .
docker volume rm nebu-minio_data 2>/dev/null; docker volume ls | grep minio; echo done
